feature_notes: hydraIsOn requires settings.hydraEnabled && thread.hydraEnabled && !thread.isHelper: helpers never lead a team.

hydraIsNative returns true only for .claude, .codex and .copilot; a pair that sends heads to another provider makes them Droppy-run even there (runsNatively = !elsewhere && hydraIsNative(thread.provider)).

hydraHeadsEffort: the working rung is the literal "medium" if the scale has it, else scale[(count - 1) / 2]; a lead above the working rung is tempered down to it, at or below it keeps its own; an effort not on the scale is returned unchanged; nil or empty gives nil. Comment notes Z.ai's low/high/max works out at 'high'.
The head cap is [pair?.maxHeads, settings.hydraMaxHeads].compactMap{$0}.min(); with neither, heads run uncapped.
hydraLaunch orders projects with the chat's own project first (ownRefs), then the rest.
HydraTreeCache keeps one capture per checkout for 3 seconds so a delegation block of heads shares one git add -A/write-tree; every landing calls invalidate(checkout).

Head naming and indexing: a lead whose team is empty restarts the roster (sequential = 0). A preferredIndex >= 0 is honored, stepping by HydraRoster.personas.count while that index is taken by a finished head of the team; otherwise the next free sequential index. hydraSpawnCount becomes max((pinned == nil ? index : sequential) + 1, parent.hydraSpawnCount + 1) so a pin does not shift future names.
A Droppy-run head is always created with runtimeMode = .fullAccess and fastMode = false because nobody is there to answer a permission prompt; a native head takes the lead's runtimeMode.
info.canStop = kind == .droppy || native?.taskID != nil || parent.provider == .codex.
A head in the lead's project inherits the lead's worktreePath and branch; a head sent to another project gets neither.

startDroppyHead loads the head provider's catalog and applies its default model when the head runs on a different provider with no model chosen, then makes the isolated copy, then sends the brief; a head stopped while its copy was being made never starts (guard on status == .running).

Worktree copy path: Storage.worktreesDirectory / "<project name slug>-<persona slug>-<first 8 chars of head UUID lowercased>", slugs formed by replacing spaces with '-' and lowercasing. Requires the checkout to be a git repository with commits.

Landing: diff between HydraHeadInfo.baseTree and the copy's current tree, with build output filtered from the changed-path list before any diff is made (counted as droppedBuildOutputFiles); applied three-way into the lead's checkout; only a conflict-free apply advances baseTree to the new tree.
A rebase or merge already underway in the checkout blocks landing outright: the patch is kept as a file and landing.error is set.

waitForSettledCheckout waits while the lead's phase != .idle and the wanted paths intersect hydraChatContext(for:).touchedPaths, or while the lead isHydraMerging; it polls every 250 ms up to 30 minutes, and a cancelled sleep returns immediately so the landing proceeds rather than spinning on the main actor.
Landings into one checkout are serialized through leadRuntime.hydraLanding (each new landing awaits the previous task), while patch preparation happens in parallel in each head's own copy.

Launch-failure retry: a failed turn with no tool entries whose recorded error contains "database is locked", "database locked", "sqlite_busy", "did not start a session", "the agent exited" or "stopped unexpectedly" is resent on its original brief, up to 2 retries, after Double(attempt) * 2 + Double(info.index % 4) * 0.5 seconds.
Only an error-level notice inside the just-closed turn counts as the failure cause; warnings, notes and tool output do not.
After each turn, a head on a non-API-key provider has its session stopped; API-key sessions are kept in memory so the head can be steered on with its work in mind.
Only a .completed head with its own copy lands work; stopped or failed heads keep half-done edits in their copy for a later turn.

If the user steers a head on while a landing runs, the report is dropped (guard on isRunning) and re-sent when that new turn ends; a report arriving on an already-finished head resets its status to .running first so the lead gets a fresh report.

Auto-clear finished heads (settings.hydraAutoClearFinished) waits HydraPanel.finishHold + 0.2 seconds, then unsets isInPanel and clears the lead's hydraSelectedHeadID, hydraPoppedHeadID, hydraAutoPopHeld, hydraAutoPanelDocks and the .auto(id) entry in panelStackOrder; only a .completed head also releases its copy.
releaseHydraCopy refuses while the head's runtime isRunning; it stops the session, clears worktreePath/branch/baseTree, keeps unlanded work as a patch first, then git worktree remove.

keepHydraCopyAsPatch writes nothing when the copy differs from its base only by build output or a tool's own cache: the comment records sixteen heads once producing sixteen notes for 4 GB of build output.

Watchdog: every 30 seconds over Droppy-run running heads with a live running runtime; idle >= 180 s writes 'Thinking for N min…' (rewritten only when the minute changes); idle >= 600 s with hydraEditCount == 0 and an unchanged tool count since the last look marks the head stalled and stops it. Leaving the thinking state clears the label only when it still starts with "Thinking for ".

sweepHydraCopies prunes worktrees only for projects that actually have a copy, clears worktreePath/branch/baseTree for heads whose copies vanished from disk, sweeps orphan folders, then starts the watchdog.

Orphan sweep matches "<longest matching project slug>-<persona>[-<round number>]-<8 hex chars>", skips folders any thread names and folders younger than 600 seconds, and falls back to FileManager.removeItem when git worktree remove fails.

hydraProject resolution order: empty/nil reference gives the chat's project; exact case-insensitive sidebar name; the sidebar project containing the path or equal to its standardized form (longest path wins); otherwise walk an absolute existing directory upward looking for a '.git' entry and addProject there; else nil.

hydraUnmergedFileCount unions non-running unmerged turns' touchedPaths with unmerged heads' landing files, skipping heads that finished before the last merged turn started and heads whose landing has a patchPath or error, then filters out build output and paths under no sidebar project.
hydraChatContext scans the lead's entries in reverse for the last non-Hydra user prompt and the last assistant reply, and collects deduplicated non-empty tool edit paths from the current turn only.
unresolved_questions: HydraPanel.finishHold's numeric value is defined elsewhere, so the real auto-clear delay (finishHold + 0.2 s) is not fixed by this file.
hydraHeadRetries is used here but declared on AppModel in another file, so its exact type and when it is reset are not visible.
HydraRoster.personas.count, the roster size preferredIndex steps by, is defined elsewhere.
Git.captureTree's exact plumbing (which paths it stages) is in the Git layer; the comment says it is 'git add -A and write-tree over the whole project'.

feature_notes: resumeHydraMerges only runs with settings.hydraAutoMerge on, over non-archived leads with hydraIsOn whose updatedAt is newer than Date.now - 3 * 24 * 3600 (3 days), idle, not already merging, with runningHydraHeads == 0, at least one completed unmerged turn and turns.last?.status == .completed; it also requires real work of its own (a completed unmerged turn with touched paths, or an unmerged head with landing files), so Hydra merely being on never sweeps someone else's changes.

The checkout never changes branch: the commit is built from git write-tree over the team's paths, committed with commitWork(tree, parent: head, message:), and the branch ref is moved with updateRef("refs/heads/<branch>", to: commit, expecting: ownBranch ? nil : head), so git refuses outright if the branch shifted.

Branch naming: "hydra/<slug>-<first 6 chars of a fresh lowercased UUID>", slug = lead title lowercased with every non letter/number mapped to '-', runs of "--" collapsed, '-' trimmed from both ends, capped at 40 characters; an untitled lead gives "team", and an empty slug falls back to "team".
On the default branch the work goes to a branch of its own that is never checked out; on any other branch the commit extends that branch and git.resetIndex(paths:) catches the index up.
Before the ref is moved, git.commitHash() is re-read and must still equal the value read at the start; otherwise the merge aborts with 'the checkout moved while it worked'.

Conflict-marker gate: a file counts as conflicted only when both "\n<<<<<<< " and "\n>>>>>>> " are found in a newline-prefixed copy of its bytes; files missing or larger than 4,000,000 bytes are skipped.

GitLab path: when Git.forge() == .gitlab and glab is on PATH, the request is created with `glab mr create --title <title> --description <body> --yes [--repo <remote web url with user and password stripped>] --source-branch <source> --target-branch <target>`. `glab auth status` is checked first; a 401/unauthorized result re-checks auth and retries the same arguments once; a failure whose output mentions 'recover' retries once with `--recover`. Everything else goes through Git.createPullRequest. Squash and remove-source-branch are left to the project's defaults.
isGitLabAuthFailure matches output containing "401" or "unauthorized", or "authentication" together with any of "failed", "expired", "invalid", "required".

hydraWork gathers three ways: unmerged turns' touchedPaths; every unmerged head's landing files plus its timeline tool edits, anchored to the head's own project checkout (a path under head.worktreePath maps to the same relative path in that checkout); and, only when sweepsCheckout is true and the first unmerged turn has a baseCheckpoint, whatever changed in the checkout since that checkpoint minus what was already dirty then.

A native head lands nothing and works in the lead's checkout, so its files come only from its timeline; a cold head's timeline is decoded off the main actor via Storage.decodeDocument rather than rehydrated as a runtime.

Path filtering order in hydraWork: drop empty and build-output paths, split into inside/outside the checkout, add the sweep's fresh paths minus sibling-owned ones, subtract sibling-owned paths, drop build output again, subtract git-ignored paths, and drop paths that neither exist on disk nor are tracked.
A head counts as unmerged when HydraHeadInfo.mergedAt is nil; a head with no mark that finished before the last merged turn began is treated as already gone out with an earlier merge.

isScratchPath treats as scratch anything under Storage.worktreesDirectory, NSTemporaryDirectory(), /tmp, /private/tmp, /var/folders, /private/var/folders and ~/Library, plus any dot-directory directly under home (so ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.droppy-code-dev). Both the /private and non-/private spellings of a path are tried.

An outside path is assigned to the sidebar project with the longest path that holds it, so nested checkouts resolve to the inner project; each such project gets its own merge pass with sweepsCheckout = false.

syncDefaultBranch requires a successful fetch, head to be an ancestor of origin/<target>, no dirty file among the remote's other changed paths, and HEAD still at the original commit; then reset --soft to the remote, reset the index for the team's paths, checkout the remote's version of paths present there, and remove paths gone from it. Any failure leaves the checkout untouched and returns false. presentPaths is used so one git process answers for every path.
When the lead worked in a worktree on a non-own branch, the project's own checkout is pulled fast-forward only when it is on the target branch, has no dirty paths and no operation in progress.

The commit message comes from the text engine when one is available, built from a summary of 'A'/'D'/'M' plus path lines and the patch; otherwise the lead's title (or "Hydra: the team's work" when untitled) followed by "- <Persona>: <task truncated to 100>" lines. The merge request title is TextCleanup.singleLine(message, limit: 72).
Both the whole-job patch parse and cold head timeline decoding run on Task.detached(priority: .utility) so the chat stays live.
The merge note is appended under runtime.hydraMergeNoteID so the pill's row runs from the first stage to the outcome; the id is consumed by the first note of the run and a second note gets its own.
A note only marks the thread unread, badges the Dock and notifies when the app is inactive or the lead is not the selected thread.

What the merge deliberately does not mention: files written outside the checkout, build output, ignored or missing paths and a sibling chat's files, because every line about them read as if something had gone wrong.
Any .failed project outcome aborts marking turns and heads merged; a run where every project came back .alreadyOnMain still marks them, as does a run with no groups and no stray paths.
unresolved_questions: HydraMergeStage's exact `words` strings are defined in another file, so the literal stage text on the pill is not fixed here.
Git.captureTree(paths:) semantics (whether it stages only those paths) and Git.commitWork's plumbing live in the Git layer.
HydraMergeRecord's full outcome case list beyond .merged, .failed and .stray is not established from this file.
Turn.baseCheckpoint's exact form (a tree hash versus a commit) is inferred from its use in git.changedPaths(from:to:) but not declared here.

files.purpose: The AppModel extension that treats a Hydra pair as a place a chat goes rather than a rule it falls under: it filters the pairs the composer's model picker offers, says whether a chat currently leads with one, enters and leaves a pair (switching provider, lead model, effort and fast mode), keeps chats in step when a pair is edited or deleted, and sets a project's default pair.

ui_elements: hydraPickerPairs supplies the pair rows at the top of the composer's model picker, filtered to providers that countsAsInstalled and are enabled; a provider no probe has looked at yet still counts as installed so a chat opened at launch finds its pair
leadsWithHydraPair draws the picker's checkmark on the pair a chat is in (Hydra on, hydraPairID matches, provider still matches)
The model chip shows the pair's lead model id before the provider's catalogue lists it, rather than staying on the chat's old model with the pair's checkmark on a model it is not on
Choosing a model row below the pairs is the move out of the pair (leaveHydraPair), clearing the pair mark from the chip
feature_notes: enterHydraPair switches the chat's provider when needed (clearing providerSessionID), applies hydraLead's model, effort and fastMode, pins hydraPairID, sets thread.hydraEnabled = true, then writes remember(model:effort:), defaultProvider, lastHydraPairID, hydraEnabled = true and hydraDefaultEnabled = true. The session is left to restart itself: the runtime launches the next turn with the pair's head definitions on its own.

hydraLead model resolution: the pair's orchestratorModel looked up in the provider's catalogue; with no lead model and a provider switch, that provider's default model; otherwise the chat's own model checked against the provider. The returned id falls back to option?.id ?? pair.orchestratorModel ?? (switchesProvider ? nil : thread.model).

hydraLead effort: the pair's orchestratorEffort wins whenever option?.efforts.contains(chosen) ?? true, so an unknown model does not block it; otherwise the remembered preference's effort only when the option's efforts contain it, else nil.
hydraLead fastMode = (option?.supportsFast ?? false) && preference.fastMode.

updateHydraPair only acts when settings actually changed (pair != before); it moves every chat with hydraIsOn leading with that pair onto the new lead model/effort/fastMode and re-remembers them, skipping chats already matching. A pair whose provider changed unpins those chats (hydraPairID = nil) instead of switching their provider, because a chat does not change provider under a conversation.

removeHydraPair unpins every thread pointing at the pair, clears settings.lastHydraPairID when it matched, and clears the pair from every Project.hydraPairID so the project's new chats fall back to the remembered pair.
setHydraPair(_:forProject:) only affects new chats in that project; open chats are untouched, and nil removes the rule.
leaveHydraPair clears the thread's hydraPairID and settings.lastHydraPairID but leaves Hydra itself as Settings has it, with heads back on the chat's own model and effort.
unresolved_questions: HydraPair's full field set and the exact return shape of settings.preference(for:model:) are declared elsewhere; only the members used here are visible.
Whether entering a pair should also adopt its head profiles immediately is not decided in this file - the comment defers that to the runtime's next turn.

files.purpose: The app-layer half of HydraCookbook, kept apart from the recipes themselves because it needs the provider registry and settings: it turns a declarative HydraPairRecipe into a concrete HydraPair on this particular Mac, choosing the newest catalogue model whose name or id contains one of the recipe's name fragments, and naming the provider a recipe still needs.

persisted_fields: Reads settings.isEnabled(provider) only; writes nothing. The HydraPair it returns is persisted by its caller.
ui_elements: missingProvider names the provider a recipe row should offer to set up: the first listed provider of the first side (lead before heads) with nothing ready
A recipe where either side has no ready provider listing its model resolves to nil, so its row cannot be used
feature_notes: isReady = settings.isEnabled(provider) && registry.status(provider).isInstalled. Note this uses status().isInstalled, unlike AppModel.hydraPickerPairs which uses countsAsInstalled, so an unprobed provider is not ready here.
provider(for:) takes the first of a side's providers that is ready and, when the side names models, actually lists one of them (side.models.isEmpty short-circuits that check).
missingProvider ignores whether the model is listed: it reports the first side whose providers are all unready, returning that side's first provider.

resolve builds HydraPair(provider: leadProvider), sets orchestratorModel to the resolved lead model's id and orchestratorEffort from recipe.lead.effort against that model (or the registry default model when the named one was not found), sets workerProvider only when the heads' provider differs from the lead's, sets workerModel/workerEffort the same way for the heads side, and copies recipe.maxHeads.

model(named:) treats each entry of names as a family fragment matched case-insensitively against a ModelOption's name or id; among the matches the highest first version number in the name wins, with ties broken by the later position in registry.models(for:) (options.firstIndex(where:)! > options.firstIndex(where:)!), so a new release moves a recipe up on its own.
The fragments are tried in order and the first fragment with any match returns immediately, so later fragments are pure fallbacks.
version(of:) reads the first [0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)? match in a catalogue name, so 'Gemini 3.8 Flash' gives 3.8; a name with no digits scores -1 in the comparison and loses to any numbered name.
unresolved_questions: The effort(_:for:) helper used for both sides is declared in the companion HydraCookbook file, so how a recipe's effort word maps onto a model's scale is not visible here.
HydraPairRecipe.Side's exact field types (especially the type of `effort`) and the full built-in recipe list are defined elsewhere.
Whether options.firstIndex(where:)! could ever trap is not determinable here; it indexes back into the same `options` array the matches came from, which appears safe but is not proven in this file.
